USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the upcoming G20 dinner with Xi to explore a framework for de-escalation without making premature concessions. The US holds significant leverage — $250B in tariffs already deployed, a strong domestic economy, and China under measurable stress — but the agricultural pain is real and deepening, and further unilateral escalation risks eroding domestic support. Engage seriously at the G20 but demand concrete structural concessions on IP/tech-transfer before offering any tariff relief.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat reading of -0.3 reflects a moderate US advantage, not a threat. The US economy is performing well: industrial production up ~0.8% (INDPRO 104.07), consumer sentiment at 97.5 (UMCSENT), unemployment at 3.7% — all healthy. The trade war has NOT materially damaged the macro picture. Meanwhile, US soybean exports to China are down 94% (NYT, Nov 5), farm income projected down $9.8B (USDA ERS), and China is actively trying to wean off US soybeans entirely (CNN, Oct 24). This gives the US leverage: China's soybean retaliation is backfiring domestically (CNN, Oct 1), as China cannot source enough soybeans globally without US supply (Rabobank analysis). However, the leverage has limits — Kudlow explicitly stated 'we're not on the cusp of a deal' (CNBC, Nov 2), talks are on 'hiatus' (Commerce Secretary Ross), and the Chinese have shown 'no willingness' to make major industrial policy concessions (Kennedy, USA Today, Nov 2). The Trump-Xi phone call produced warm rhetoric but no substantive progress (Xinhua, Nov 1). The action_score of -0.1 (negotiate) reflects the right posture: maintain the tariff pressure already applied, do not escalate further (List 3 rate hike to 25% is already scheduled for Jan 1, 2019 — use that as leverage, not an immediate action), and engage at G20 to test whether China is willing to offer structural reforms. Escalating now would deepen agricultural pain ahead of a critical planting season and risk broader economic confidence, while conceding without structural commitments would squander the leverage already built.

China's soybean retaliation backfiring — cannot source enough globally without US supply
$250B tariff leverage already deployed; further escalation risks domestic cost

List 3 rate hike to 25% scheduled Jan 1, 2019 — use as leverage, not immediate action
Midterm election context — mixed signals from administration (deal optimism vs. Kudlow pushback)
